title: Our five senses
examples: What do I use to see the colors?
How does my body know if something is hot?
Can I smell flowers with my ears?

explain.say: Today we learn about your five amazing senses. These senses help you explore the world around you. We will talk about sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
Sight lets you see bright colors and shapes. You use your eyes to look at everything. For example, you use your sight to see a big red apple.
Hearing helps you know sounds all around you. You use your ears to listen carefully. For example, you hear the sound of a barking dog.
Smell lets you know about different smells. You use your nose to sniff the air. For example, you smell the sweet scent of cookies.
Taste helps you know what food tastes like. You use your tongue to taste things. For example, you taste the sour lemon juice.
A common mistake is thinking you only use one sense at a time. You actually use many senses together all the time. For example, you might see and hear a bird singing.

faq.q: Which sense do I use to know if something is soft?
faq.a: You use your sense of touch to know if something is soft. Touch lets you feel different textures. You might also ask: What sense feels things? Or: How do I know if it is fuzzy?
asks: How do I know if it is fuzzy?

faq.q: Can my eyes help me smell things?
faq.a: No, your eyes are only for seeing things. You must use your nose to smell different things. You might also ask: Which sense is for smelling? Or: Can I see smells?

faq.q: Do I need all five senses to play?
faq.a: Yes, all five senses help you explore and play. They work together to help you learn. You might also ask: Are all senses important? Or: Can I play without my ears?
asks: Can I play without my ears?

faq.q: Is taste the same as smell?
faq.a: No, taste and smell are two different senses. Taste is what your tongue feels, and smell is what your nose detects. You might also ask: Are they related? Or: Does smelling help me taste?

faq.q: What part of my body helps me hear sounds?
faq.a: Your ears are the parts of your body that help you hear. They catch the sounds around you. You might also ask: Where do sounds come from? Or: What do I use to listen?
asks: What do I use to listen?

facts: Eyes help us see colors and shapes.
Ears help us hear loud and soft sounds.
Noses help us smell sweet and bad smells.
Tongues help us taste sweet, sour, and salty.
Skin helps us feel things like hot and cold.

quiz.say: Which sense do you use to know if ice is cold?
quiz.why: Touch lets you feel if something is cold or hot.

wrong.0: You might think sight because cold things look different.
wrong.1: You might think taste because cold things sometimes taste different.
wrong.2: You might think hearing because cold things sometimes make sounds.

quiz.say: If you smell perfume, which sense is working?
quiz.why: Smell uses your nose to detect different scents.

wrong.1: You might think sight because you see the perfume bottle.
wrong.2: You might think taste because smells can sometimes make your mouth feel something.
wrong.3: You might think touch because you might wave your hand near it.

quiz.say: When you hear music, which sense is helping you?
quiz.why: Hearing uses your ears to catch the vibrations of sound.

wrong.1: You might think sight because music videos show pictures.
wrong.2: You might think touch because you might tap your feet to the rhythm.
wrong.3: You might think smell because sometimes music has a certain 'smell' associated with it.
